summary_for_children: Al-Kahf has four stories: young believers who slept in a cave, a man proud of his two gardens, Musa's journey to learn from a knowing servant of Allah, and Dhul-Qarnayn who built a barrier.
environment_concept: Four connected adventures: the cave of the young believers, the two gardens, the meeting of the two seas, and the iron barrier.
architecture_and_scenery: Mountain cave with sunlight sliding past its mouth, two walled gardens with a river, a meeting of two seas with a ship and a leaning wall, and a pass sealed by iron and copper.

palette.atmosphere: Cool cave air, garden breeze, sea mist, mountain wind

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: Four Extraordinary Journeys
story_library.children_narration: Surah Al-Kahf contains several remarkable journeys. First, a group of young believers sought refuge in a cave. Allah caused them to sleep for many years. Then we hear about two men and their gardens, reminding us that wealth should never make us proud. Next comes Musa's journey with a knowledgeable servant of Allah. Musa learns that some events have wisdom he does not understand at first. Finally, Dhul-Qarnayn travels across different lands and helps a community by building a strong barrier. Each journey teaches something special about faith, humility, knowledge, and responsibility.

world_idea.title: The Four Realms
world_idea.description: Four distinct adventures: an explorable cave, two contrasting gardens, a journey through coastal locations, and a barrier-engineering activity inspired by 18:93–98.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: The young men of the cave, Musa, al-Khidr and Dhul-Qarnayn are not shown. The boy in 18:74 and 18:80 is reading only, with no scene.
